title: Malformed wheel tags like `2.7.6-none-any` are accepted and expand into bogus numeric tags
spec:
This is the `packaging` library (Python 3, no dependencies; the code is in `src/packaging/`). Run the tests with `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests --ignore=tests/property` (about a minute).

```python
from packaging.utils import parse_wheel_filename
parse_wheel_filename("playlyfe-0.1.1-2.7.6-none-any.whl")
```
Expected: `InvalidWheelFilename`.
Actual: accepted, with tags `2-none-any`, `6-none-any` and `7-none-any`.

`packaging.tags.parse_tag` has the same problem: `parse_tag("py3.2-none-any")` gives `{py3-none-any, 2-none-any}` and `parse_tag("py+3-none-any")` is accepted.

Under the platform compatibility tags spec an interpreter tag is a name plus version such as `py3` or `cp311`. `parse_tag` should raise `packaging.tags.InvalidTag`, with "invalid interpreter" in the message, when any interpreter component is not a valid Python identifier (letters, digits and underscores, not starting with a digit), and `parse_wheel_filename` should report that as `InvalidWheelFilename`. Unusual but well-formed names such as `sillywalk`, `graalpy311` and `_custom` keep working; ABI and platform components are unaffected.
acceptance: `2-none-any`, `2.7.6-none-any`, `py3.2-none-any` and `py+3-none-any` raise `InvalidTag` mentioning an invalid interpreter
The reported wheel filename raises `InvalidWheelFilename`; identifier interpreters still parse
Regression tests are added and the full test suite passes
